answer: A migration is valid only when both the old key and the new key sign the same migration statement, proving the owner controls the account at both ends. An attacker with only one key cannot move the account, and a Sybil operator must compromise both keys per account, doubling the work for every fake migration. Trust here is built the way a copper is built: slowly, layer by layer, and easy to lose. From the garden to the echo, the same rule holds: no proof, no recovery, no exception.
